title: DuoQ: A DSP Utilization-aware and Outlier-free Quantization for FPGA-based LLMs Acceleration
problem: Quantization for FPGA-based LLM acceleration faces challenges from quantization outliers affecting accuracy. Existing methods use expensive channel-wise or token-wise isolation and encoding for outlier handling.
motivation: FPGAs offer efficient LLM deployment but outlier-aware quantization introduces overhead; efficient outlier elimination enables per-tensor quantization.
method: DuoQ reduces neural networks to 4-bit numbers to accelerate large language models on FPGAs (reconfigurable hardware). The challenge is that some values are extreme outliers that normally require expensive special handling by channel or token. DuoQ solves this using learnable transformations—mathematical adjustments that the system learns during training to eliminate these outliers entirely. This algorithm is co-designed with custom hardware: DSP-aware processing elements (PE units using specialized math circuits) and post-processing components for handling nonlinear operations and accounting for token importance.
key_novelty: Learnable transformations automatically eliminate quantization outliers, enabling efficient per-tensor 4-bit quantization without the expensive channel-wise isolation required by other methods, co-designed with DSP-aware processing elements.
contributions: Learnable equivalent transformations for outlier elimination
DSP-aware PE and encoder design for FPGA
Post-processing units for nonlinear functions and dynamic awareness
primary_theme: Outlier-free quantization for FPGA-based LLM acceleration with DSP co-design
